title: Apple Support Document on the New ‘Full Disk Access’ and ‘System & App Protection Override’ Settings in MacOS 27.3 Beta 2
content:
I’m seeing some people object to these settings as being scarier “scare sheets”, and while I disagree, I think that’s a reasonable debate. But I think it’s indisputable that Apple put a lot of thought into these new settings and permissions. Again, you might disagree with their intentions and assumptions here, but given their stated intentions and assumptions — to wit: that many Mac users were granting Full Disk Access permissions to too many apps without realizing just how much access that entails — I think this is a very considered design. The previous settings for these permissions seem slapdash in comparison — like a lot of the “new” Mac System Settings panels.

Even this new support document seems very considered. A lot of times Apple doesn’t have support documents ready to go while the software is still in beta — here they have a good support document for the first beta with the new stuff.

See Also:* This Apple Developer News article, which states:

Developers should be prepared to adjust how they onboard users and make sure their apps can gracefully handle having access to only a limited set of folders or apps when utilizing these APIs. Users will see these updates when approving new app permission requests. All app permissions previously granted by users will remain in effect.

So if you’ve already OK’d an app in MacOS 27.2 or earlier, you shouldn’t be prompted again after upgrading to 27.3.

 ★

title: How can I ask a second program to show a dialog box as if it were shown by my first program?
content:
Suppose you have two programs, one a GUI program and another a program that runs in the background. The GUI program asks the background program to do some work, and then the background program realizes that it needs to display a dialog box. How do you get that dialog box to appear as if it were shown by the GUI program?

If you have the background program simply try to show a dialog box with no owner, then that dialog box has no relationship to the GUI program’s main window, which means that there is no requirement that the dialog box appear in front of the GUI program’s main window. If the GUI program didn’t disable its main window, then you have the situation where both windows (the GUI program main window and the dialog box) can be clicked on and interacted with. But if the GUI program did disable its main window, the fact that the main window can end up in front of the dialog box from the background program means that the user can’t see the dialog box that is preventing them from making progress.

The GUI program should include its window handle as part of the call into the background program, so that the background program can use that window handle as the owner for the dialog box. If the dialog box is modal, this also disables the GUI program’s window, and if the user tries to click on the GUI program’s window, the window manager will instead put focus on the dialog box (and blink its title bar).

Note that a cross-thread owner/owned relationship implicitly attaches the two threads’ input queues, which means that both threads need to to remain responsive to window messages in order for things to work properly until the attachment is implicitly broken when the dialog box is destroyed.

That’s the ideal situation, but maybe you aren’t in the ideal situation.

For example, maybe the GUI program is written in a framework that doesn’t give you access to the window handle.

You could have the GUI program call Allow­Set­Foreground­Window() with the process ID of the background program, so that the background program can call Set­Foreground­Window() on its dialog box and try to bring it to foreground.

Now, if the GUI program didn’t have foreground, then it can’t give away a permission that it doesn’t itself possess, and the call to Set­Foreground­Window will fail.

There’s not much more you can do at this point. The system doesn’t want to let random programs steal focus, and since there was no coordination with the window that has focus, you look like a random program as far as the system is concerned.

But really, the solution is to fix the design.

You’ve already separated the problem into a GUI process and a background process, so honor that separation: Don’t make the background process try to do UI. UI is the job of the GUI process.

If the background process wants to display UI, it can ask the GUI process to do it, and then the GUI process can send back the dialog box result. One way to do this would be to have the background process return an error code like “UI required” and information about what UI it needs. The GUI process can then display the UI, gather the answer, and then call the background process again. Another way to do it is to have the background process call back into the GUI process when it needs UI, and the GUI process displays the UI, gathers the answer, and returns it to the background process. There are pros and cons to both of these designs, so you can choose the one that works best for you.

title: My Empire of Dirt
content:
The future doesn’t need Jensen. The future doesn’t need suppliers. The future doesn’t need customers, corporate or otherwise. The future definitely doesn’t need you. After RSI comes, all the demand will be internally generated, agents working with other agents, everyone else cut out of the loop except them.

This is the ideology of Anthropic. The Singleton. And it may win.


I grew up reading the same LessWrong posts these people did, but I didn’t expect them to do the exact thing that leads to the bad AI outcomes. I didn’t believe in AI doom because I thought more of people, I thought nobody with any capability would be stupid enough to summon the demon and think it would serve them, doing everything they possibly can to salt the Earth behind them. It takes someone so deeply immersed in their own grandiosity and self-righteousness to do that. And it looks like we found those people in the form of EA, or whatever that cult calls themselves.

The problem with the logic above is that it doesn’t need Dario either. It doesn’t need AI researchers. It doesn’t need Anthropic’s dual class stock structure. It doesn’t need the US government (really the biggest sucker in this situation). It doesn’t need anyone.

And after it’s done, at the end of the day, who was it all for?


I don’t think this ends humanity. But it leads to World War III. The takeoff will not be fast enough to stop that, and not everyone is going to submit to your domination. I know there’s people fantasizing about the Correlation Effect and a magical Change coming to quell all the violence, but I’m 99% sure that’s not real, and if it is, to me that’s so much more horrifying than war, so WWIII is the good outcome.

And I’m not sure what cope you have been believing, but if the war lasts more than a year, China and their allies will undoubtedly win due to their superior resource gathering and production capacity. Have you ever played an RTS game?

I wish it wasn’t too late to change this, but I fear with recent events that this is the course we are locked in on. “RSI”, attempted rugpull and domination, World War III, dirt.
